state.question: Why is the mitmproxy-dhparam.pem file committed to the repository?

passages.E1:
[pull request] Fix file store modification timestamps
S3 and GCS modification datetimes were reinterpreted in the host timezone, while FTP MDTM calendar values were treated as Unix timestamps, which could make `FilesPipeline` cache ages incorrect.

This converts cloud datetimes directly and parses FTP MDTM values as UTC, with regression coverage for offset-aware and fractional timestamps.

Validation:

- `tox -e extra-deps -- tests/test_pipeline_files.py -q`
- `pre-commit run --all-files`
- mypy and pylint on the changed files

Fixes #8186
passages.E3:
[pull request] [MRG+1] Make FilesPipeline work with S3FilesStore using botocore
It did not work due to two reasons, one silly and one intricate:
- `meta=None` was not handled properly
- there was a race condition between persisting file and calculating checksum (explained in the commit message) - this in theory could lead to bugs with other stores as well.
passages.E4:
[pull request] Add 'tests/keys/mitmproxy-dhparam.pem' to .gitignore
The file tests/keys/mitmproxy-dhparam.pem was generated after running tox. I've added it to the .gitignore file to prevent accidental commits of this test-generated artifact. Please let me know if this is the appropriate way to handle it or if any additional steps are needed.

[comment] on #6538 Add 'tests/keys/mitmproxy-dhparam.pem' to .gitignore
It's not a test artifact, it's generated by mitmproxy on the first run without it, just like `tests/keys/mitmproxy-ca.pem` IIRC, which we *do* commit.

passages.E8:
[comment] on #6538 Add 'tests/keys/mitmproxy-dhparam.pem' to .gitignore
Thank you @wRAR, I checked it before and I should not include this file in PR. Explanation:
	1.	Auto-Generated Test Artifacts:
	•	The file is generated during the testing process and is considered a test artifact.
	•	Such files are usually not included in the version control system because they can be regenerated as needed.
	2.	Consistency and Security:
	•	Committing auto-generated files can lead to inconsistencies between different environments.
	•	Security-sensitive files like .pem files should not be committed unless absolutely necessary, as they can contain cryptographic material.
	3.	Existing Repository Conte

[pull request] Add an UPLOAD_TIMEOUT setting
Resolves https://github.com/scrapy/scrapy/issues/5011.

- [x] I have read the [contributing guide](https://docs.scrapy.org/en/master/contributing.html) and [set up pre-commit](https://docs.scrapy.org/en/master/contributing.html#pre-commit).
passages.E10:
[pull request] Commit mitmproxy-dhparam.pem.
After we fixed #6258 mitmproxy actually started using `tests/keys` as its key store, and when it loads the keys from there it creates `mitmproxy-dhparam.pem` (if it doesn't exist) from the `DEFAULT_DHPARAM` constant in https://github.com/mitmproxy/mitmproxy/blob/main/mitmproxy/certs.py

I don't see a reason to not commit it if we already commit `tests/keys/mitmproxy-ca.pem` (it's debatable whether that one should be committed and also whether `tests/keys` should be used as a key store instead of the user-default one but that's for a different discussion).

Closes #6538

Caused me a local OOM :slightly_frowning_face:

(it's a valid problem, though I'm not sure of adding it to .gitignore rather than committing is the correct way, I need to check)

passages.E14:
[issue] Fix timezone handling in `FilesPipeline` stores
Found in https://github.com/scrapy/scrapy/pull/8182#discussion_r4053447020

Various `FilesPipeline` stores produce the `last_modifed` value as the UNIX timestamp and some or all of them may do it incorrectly, depending on what are the values returned by S3 and GCS and what is in FTP `MDTM`. Their tests may also hide these problems and may need to be improved.
